deep.reconstruction: There are no mathematical derivations on this page. It continues the preceding page's aphoristic notes on 'Anschauung' (intuition) and on the value of knowledge. The previous page ends with: 'Vielleicht ...'. This page continues 'das freihändige Zeichnen?', i.e. perhaps freehand drawing trains intuition. The notes are as follows. (1) On intuition and drawing: it is far from being draughtsmanship ('Fabriken-zeichnen') if the object does not present itself to the eye in that way. There are other representations ('Abbildungen') than linear ones through sight, and schematic drawing is often much more advantageous and more vivid. 'Auditory thinking', because one-dimensional (beat/rhythm, 'Takt'). This continues the previous page's taxonomy of geometric, arithmetic, mechanical and physiological intuition, which cites Helmholtz, Vorträge und Reden I, pp. 173-174. Implicitly, sight gives a two- or three-dimensional representation while hearing gives a one-dimensional, time-ordered one. (2) On usefulness: every knowledge and skill, even alchemy, is useful; the only question is whether acquiring it pays. A joke example: swimming is very useful to the mathematician if, on a pleasure trip of the Norddeutscher Lloyd, all mathematicians fall into the water and can only save themselves by swimming. The next page continues the theme with the soldier who shoots well. (3) The Italians favour the general and the principled in science, pursued with great enthusiasm, which is 'very sympathetic to me'. (4) A self-description of method: details confuse and repel him; they gain interest only through the principled point of view. But then he prefers carrying the argument out in a special case, as the simpler route. A phrase 'und doch ge...' is struck out.

results.what: Classification of kinds of intuition (visual/schematic drawing vs. auditory, one-dimensional 'Takt' thinking), continuing notes on geometric, arithmetic and mechanical Anschauung after Helmholtz

results.what: Methodological maxim: interest in details comes only from the general principle, but the actual proof is best carried out in a special case as the simpler route

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds personal aphorisms on intuition, pedagogy and method with no mathematics. They fit Hilbert's known views on Anschauung and his known heuristic of working in special cases. The Italian and swimming remarks add mild biographical colour only.
transcription_corrections: 'Norddeutsch. Loyd[?]' should be 'Norddeutsch. Lloyd' (the Norddeutscher Lloyd shipping line); the hand reads roughly 'Logd'.
'Entusiasmus' is Hilbert's own spelling (no 'h'); keep as written.
The struck-out word after 'verwirren mich und' is plausibly 'machen', but it is illegible; the uncertainty mark is appropriate.
The first word on the page is 'das' (lowercase), continuing 'Vielleicht' from the previous page: 'Vielleicht das freihändige Zeichnen?'.
The marker '*' before 'Fabriken-' and before 'Jede Kenntniss' appears as a struck or crossed symbol, likely an insertion or cross-reference mark rather than text.
